properties.name: A sentence the extraction could not place has a home (Fragment), and the served instructions finally name the tool that answers "does this already exist?"
properties.rationale:
Anthony's word, 2026-09-22, approving both together because they are the same shape: vocabulary that already existed with nothing pointing at it.

F25 IS THE `EVOLVES_INTO` STORY AGAIN AND flo2 NAMED IT AS SUCH. `Fragment` with `fragment_type: note` has always been able to hold an unplaced utterance; `grep` found no mention of it in capture-intent, so the clauses an extraction cannot place were rendered once in a transcript and lost — and those are, in their words, "the single best material for the next question to put to the person". They asked for the cheap fix (a sentence in the skill) over the expensive one (a named tool). This is the cheap fix.

THE SECOND CHANGE IS THE ONE WITH FOUR MEASURED INSTANCES BEHIND IT. flo2 built four things reflow2 already served — skill `audience`, skill `summary`, the loop-finding subject/record split, and `ingest_step` + `topic_report` — concluding "reflow2 should add X" each time. Their diagnosis: "the residue is not capability, it is REFLEX. Nothing prompts a consumer to run `find_tools` BEFORE building." Confirmed here 2026-09-22: neither `find_tools` nor `find_skills` appeared anywhere in the served working instructions. The line now sits in "The one rule", which is the first substantive thing a consumer reads.

⭐ THE DISCRIMINATION GATE EARNED ITS KEEP AGAIN, UNPROMPTED. Adding a row routing to Fragment made Fragment a routed type, and `check_discrimination_rules.py` immediately failed because Fragment declared no rules — exactly the drift it was built for, caught within a minute of being created rather than by a reader noticing months later. That is the second time in two days it has caught a real disagreement nobody seeded.

AND THE SKILL LINT CAUGHT A SECOND ONE: it read flo2's field name `unmatched`, written in backticks, as a served tool that does not exist. Rather than add another project's vocabulary to reflow2's exemption list, the phrase was reworded in BOTH the skill and the schema cue — they have to move together, because the discrimination gate compares them.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: Two one-line changes closing the last two items on flo2's connector list. (1) F25: capture-intent's routing table gains a row sending an unplaceable sentence to a Fragment with `fragment_type: note`, and the schema gains Fragment's discrimination block so a consumer reading the schema sees the same rule. (2) The meta-point from the same report: `getting-started/AGENTS.md` — the working instructions every consumer is served — now tells a reader to ask whether a thing already exists before building it, naming `find_tools` and `find_skills`. Neither word appeared anywhere in that document before today.
